'''Malleus''', who was originally known as '''Telloti Cillmam'n''', was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] from [[Taanab/Legends|Taanab]]. [[Reproduction/Legends|Born]] during the last [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], he was detected by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] at a young age and sent to be [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as a member of the [[Boma Clan]] of [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Initiates]]. At the age of thirteen, he fought in the [[Jedi Temple Apprentice Tournament|Apprentice Tournament]] to attract the attention of a potential [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]. Failing to be selected, he was subsequently deemed too old to become a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan learner]]. As was customary, he was forced to join the ranks of the [[Exploration Corps/Legends|Exploration Corps]] instead.

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], after seven years of service in the Corps, Cillmam'n was dispatched to [[Nicht Ka]] with Master [[Ekim Ryelli]] and [[Staguu Itincoovar]]. Once there, he found the [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] of the ancient [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Warb Null]]. After donning the armor, Cillmam'n was flooded with visions that made him turn to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. Carried away by his newfound power, he [[Duel on Nicht Ka|dueled]] Ryelli, whom he ended up killing by [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitation]], and, after disposing of Itincoovar as well, he left the planet. Now a Dark Jedi himself, Cillmam'n assumed the identity of Malleus, the [[Hammer of the Dark Side]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Why did you choose Lumas over me that day, Master Ryelli? What did you see in him that you didn't see in me?|Cillmam'n to Ryelli|<ref name="SWI" />}}
[[File:Lumas_Etima.jpg|thumb|left|Lumas Etima became Cillmam'n's rival at the Jedi Temple.]]
A native of the [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] of [[Taanab/Legends|Taanab]]<ref name="SWI" /> in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Telloti Cillmam'n was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]], during the waning [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. He was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|keenly atuned]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="SWI" /> a mystical energy field that sprung from all lifeforms.<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> The [[Youngling/Legends|infant's]] potential attracted the attention of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]],<ref name="SWI" /> an ancient order of protectors unified by their belief and observance of the Force.<ref name="AGTSWU2" /> As was traditional among the Jedi,<ref name="TPMN">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' (novel)]]</ref> Cillmam'n was taken from his family to undergo [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the Republic and seat of the Jedi Order.<ref name="SWI" />

He grew up in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], where he was sorted in the [[Boma Clan]]&mdash;one of several [[Clan (Jedi)/Legends|groupings]] of [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi Initiates]] that were designed to appeal to the traits of their members. His classmates included another male Human, [[Lumas Etima]], with whom the Taanab-born youngling would later develop a rivalry. As all members of the Boma Clan, Cillmam'n<ref name="SWI" /> enjoyed the personal attention of [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the Order, who gave them [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] instructional courses.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> Like most Jedi initiates, he did not remember anything about his [[Parent/Legends|parents]] or [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. As a child, he maintained good relations with [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]] and [[Jocasta Nu/Legends|Jocasta Nu]], both senior [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]], who would tell him tales of the Jedi clashing with [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] in the days of old. Piell's stories in particular thrilled the young Human, who began to dream that he too would be remembered in history.<ref name="SWI" />

===Reassignment===
{{Quote|If I'd been at your side on Geonosis, there'd be no war now. I would've killed Dooku. I would've crushed the Confederacy in its cradle.|Cillmam'n to Ryelli|<ref name="SWI" />}}
[[File:Jedi_explorers.png|thumb|250px|The Exploration Corps was the archaeological branch of the Jedi Service Corps.]]
As was custom in the Order, an initiate had to attract the attention of a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and become a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan learner]] when he or she achieved the age of thirteen. Otherwise, he or she would be considered too old to proceed in his or her advanced training.<ref name="TJP" /> In [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]], Cillmam'n participated in the Jedi Temple's [[Standard year/Legends|annual]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Jedi Temple Apprentice Tournament|tournament]] as part of the [[Initiate Trials/Legends|Apprentice Trials]]. He hoped that, by exhibiting his combat skills and Force talents, he would be able to catch a Master's eye. During the tournament, Cillmam'n bested most of his fellow younglings, including Lumas Etima. In spite of that, no Jedi Master claimed him as Padawan. On top of that, Cillmam'n bitterly witnessed Etima, whom he had dueled and defeated, being chosen by Master [[Ekim Ryelli]]. Like many other washouts, he was transferred by the [[Council of Reassignment/Legends|Council of Reassignment]] to the [[Exploration Corps/Legends|Exploration Corps]], a branch of the [[Jedi Service Corps/Legends|Jedi Service Corps]], where his talents would be used for [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeology]] and [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] rather then defending the galaxy with a lightsaber. Meanwhile, the teaching relationship between Ryelli and Etima was cut short when the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. While the two were [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|fighting]] the [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], the apprentice ended up being killed whereas the master lost three fingers on his left hand. That traumatic incident reinforced Cillmam'n's opinion that he should have been chosen instead of Etima. As for Ryelli, he retired from combat and became a [[Jedi archaeologist]].<ref name="SWI" />

===Becoming the Hammer===
{{Quote|As a matter of fact, you've only been right about one thing, Master. This ''is'' a tomb.|Cillmam'n to Ryelli|<ref name="SWI" />}}
[[File:Malleus.png|thumb|left|Warb Null's armor filled Cillmam'n with visions.]]
From 26 to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Cillmam'n [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] a [[Pathfinder (Jedi)|Pathfinder]] [[Scout ship/Legends|scout vessel]] in the Exploration Corps, although he did it with lingering bitterness and disappointment. In 19 BBY, while the Clone Wars were drawing to a close, Cillmam'n was tasked with accompanying Master Ryelli to [[Nicht Ka]], an [[Ammonia/Legends|ammonia]]-washed world located on the border of the ancient [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], along with the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogator]] [[Staguu Itincoovar]]. Once the Jedi explorers had set foot into the ruins, the archaeologist started examining a few peculiar carvings on the walls. After sending Itincoovar back to their ship so he could do some philological research and help decipher the carvings, Ryelli allowed Cillmam'n to look around the place in the mean time. In another room, the young pilot came across an antique [[Armor/Legends|armor]] that had once belonged to [[Warb Null]],<ref name="SWI" /> [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] and [[Metallurgy/Legends|metallurgist]] extraordinaire, whose brief reign of terror had been ended by the Jedi [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] in [[3998 BBY]].<ref name="FNU1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]]</ref> The suit was complete, except for the missing right [[Glove/Legends|glove]], and came with a special, [[long-handle lightsaber]]. Feeling a strange fascination for that artifact, Cillmam'n put on the entire suit of armor, and was instantly flooded with visions and voices of the ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] history, including the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Invasion of Korriban|invasion]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and Sith warriors under the command of [[Sith King|King]] [[Adas]], the Sith Empire's [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Hyperspace War)|invasion of Coruscant]] under the command of [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], Warb Null forging his armor, and the death of the Dark Jedi at the hand of Ulic Qel-Droma. With the strength of that armor, the young man thought he could bring an end to the Clone Wars on his own by killing [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], leader of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist Confederacy]] that fought against the Republic.<ref name="SWI" />

When Master Ryelli found him, the corruption of the dark side had already tightened its grip on Cillmam'n, who refused to take the armor off. He [[Duel on Nicht Ka|confronted]] the archaelogist, asking the question that had haunted him for seven years: why he had chosen Etima rather than him. As Ryelli refused to answer, Cillmam'n started blaming him for not having brought the ongoing war to an end when he had the occasion. To the chagrin of Ryelli, the two then engaged in a violent [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]]. Using the hidden, secondary blade of Null's weapon, Cillmam'n ended up [[Sai cha/Legends|beheading]] the Jedi archaeologist. At the very moment that Ekim Ryelli breathed his last, Itincoovar tried to contact him via [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] to announce that the Clone Wars had been won by the Republic and that all Jedi were called back to Coruscant by the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] himself. Cillmam'n got to the Pathfinder and, after disposing of the Givin astrogator, elected to leave the planet. Although he briefly considered returning to Coruscant as the Chancellor's message ordered, he finally opted not to, since he did not consider himself a Jedi anymore. Now a follower of the dark ways, he renamed himself Malleus, the [[Hammer of the Dark Side]], and felt ready to impose his law on the whole galaxy.<ref name="SWI" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Telloti_and_Ekim.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryelli and Cillmam'n on Nicht Ka]]
{{Quote|You're afraid, now, aren't you? Were you afraid on Geonosis? Is that why Lumas died?|Cillmam'n to Ryelli|<ref name="SWI" />}}
Telloti Cillmam'n was a [[Color/Legends|brown]]-skinned man sporting black, frizzy [[Hair/Legends|hair]] which he styled in a large, rounded shape. His [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], although originally brown, turned a [[Sulfur/Legends|sulfuric]] yellow with the corruption of the dark side. From a very tender age, when he was studying at the Temple, Cillmam'n had a thirst to prove himself. He wished nothing more than becoming one of those legendary warriors he had heard about in the tales of Even Piell and Jocasta Nu. When Etima was chosen as a Jedi apprentice instead of him, Cillmam'n was very affected, and he harbored a lasting resentment toward Master Ryelli from that moment on. Bitter and craving for greatness, Cillmam'n's troubled mind offered fertile ground for the dark side of the Force.<ref name="SWI" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Part of the inspiration for Telloti's personality was, believe it or not, George C. Scott's portrayal of George S. Patton in the titular movie, ''Patton''.|Edward M. Erdelac|<ref name="hmt">{{WordPress|subdomain=emerdelac|url=2014/01/21/hammer-time-star-wars-insider-148|text=''Hammer Time! Star Wars Insider #147''|name=Delirium Tremens: The Blog of Author Edward M. Erdelac|archivedate=20230608155332}}</ref>}}
Telloti Cillmam'n, alias Malleus, was created ''[[Star Wars]]'' author [[Edward M. Erdelac]] for use in [[Hammer (short story)|''Hammer'']], a short story written for the [[Star Wars Insider 147|147th issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine. The narrative was illustrated throughout by [[Joe Corroney]], with the help of the colorist [[Brian Miller]].<ref name="SWI" /> The character was intended to be only a few years older than [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], a well known example of a Jedi<ref name="Facebook" /> who fell to the dark side around the same time.<ref name="TEA" /> In Latin, the substantive ''malleus, mallei'' literally means "hammer" or "mallet,"<ref name="maul">{{WebCite|url=http://catholic.archives.nd.edu/cgi-bin/lookup.pl?stem=malleus&ending=|text=Malleus -i|work=University of Notre Dame Latin Dictionary and Grammar Aid|nobackup=1}}</ref> which fits that character's self-awarded epithet of "Hammer of the Dark Side."<ref name="SWI" />

[[File:Patton.png|thumb|George C. Scott's portrayal of Patton inspired the character of Malleus.]]
On his personal blog, Erdelac commented that Cillmam'n's personality was partly inspired by [[Wikipedia:George C. Scott|George C. Scott's]] portrayal of the U.S. General [[Wikipedia:George S. Patton|George S. Patton]] in the [[1970]] titular movie [[Wikipedia:Patton (movie)|''Patton'']]. Like the movie's hero, Cillmam'n is frustrated at being sidestepped by history. Being a failed Jedi apprentice who finds himself under the direction of a disheartened warrior, Cillmam'ns understands that his dreams of glory are destined to fail, which ultimately paves his way to the dark side.<ref name="hmt" /> On his Facebook account, Erdelac also commented that he and his editor were "hopeful for more Malleus in the future."<ref name="Facebook" /> However, on [[April 25]], [[2014]], [[Lucasfilm]] announced that the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] was being reorganized under the new non-canon "''Star Wars'' Legends" banner to make way for a new line of continuity, led by principle projects ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' and the ''Star Wars'' [[sequel trilogy]], to take shape.<ref name="Legends">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref>
